Progressive stock faces cautious 2027 outlook from Evercore ISI
sum: Progressive stock is facing a more cautious 2027 outlook after Evercore ISI maintained an In Line rating and a 230 US dollar price target on November 2, according to Investing.com.

Evercore said clues in Progressive's 10-Q indicated that the September decline in policies in force was driven more by fewer new applications than by worsening retention. Retention nevertheless continued to deteriorate, keeping policy growth at the center of the investment case.

The research firm said agentic shopping has not yet meaningfully affected personal auto insurance. It expects the direct channel to show the impact through retention metrics if that trend gains force. Evercore also observed an improvement in the second derivative of retention in Progressive's direct channel during the third quarter.

Progressive's third-quarter filing showed stronger insurance operations alongside weaker reported earnings. Net premiums earned rose 5 percent year over year to 21.869 billion US dollars, while the companywide underwriting profit margin improved to 11.3 percent from 10.5 percent.

Net income fell to 2.542 billion US dollars from 2.615 billion US dollars in the year-earlier quarter. Net unrealized losses on fixed-maturity securities reached 1.898 billion US dollars, weighing on comprehensive income.

Progressive stock traded at 205.05 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:34 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. That was 3.85 percent below the 213.25-euro quote at 16:12 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026, in the latest AD HOC NEWS report.

For investors, the key tension is the balance between underwriting discipline and slower policy momentum. Evercore said Progressive could become more attractive in 2027 if attention shifts toward a return to earnings-per-share growth in 2028, while the firm currently sees 5 percent downside to its 2027 estimates.

Progressive stock faces mixed Q3 as underwriting gains offset losses
sum: Progressive Corp's third-quarter results, filed on Monday, November 2, 2026, showed a widening gap between insurance operations and investment performance. The insurer's Form 10-Q reported higher premiums and a stronger underwriting margin, while securities losses pulled down the bottom line.

Net premiums written increased 4 percent year over year to USD 22.3 billion, and net premiums earned rose 5 percent to USD 21.869 billion. Total revenue reached USD 23.192 billion, compared with USD 22.512 billion in the prior-year quarter.

Companywide underwriting profit margin improved to 11.3 percent from 10.5 percent a year earlier. The combined ratio fell to 88.7 from 89.5, indicating that claims and operating costs consumed a smaller share of premiums.

Personal Lines delivered a 12.0 percent underwriting margin, up from 10.5 percent. Commercial Lines remained a growth engine, with net premiums written increasing 9 percent, but its underwriting margin declined to 7.4 percent from 10.8 percent. The figures show that Progressive is still expanding across both businesses, although the quality of that growth is not uniform.

Investment performance provided the main counterweight. Progressive recorded USD 170 million in net realized securities losses, versus a USD 295 million gain in the year-earlier quarter. The company also recorded USD 1.898 billion in unrealized losses on fixed-maturity securities, compared with a USD 284 million gain previously.

Net income fell to USD 2.542 billion, or USD 4.37 per diluted share, from USD 2.615 billion, or USD 4.45 per share. Comprehensive income dropped to USD 645 million from USD 2.899 billion, reflecting the sharp swing in fixed-maturity valuations.

Policies in force increased 6 percent to 40.5 million at the end of September. Progressive said growth continued at a more moderate pace amid increased competition, while the filing showed that the company maintained profitability above its calendar-year underwriting profit goal of 4 percent.

Kansas, Steve Hackett, Big Big Train And Asia Lead Six-Night 'Cruise To The Edge 2027' Progressive Rock Adventure
sum: Progressive rock fans are going to need more than a weekend to take in this lineup. ‘Cruise To The Edge 2027’ is expanding to six nights for the first time, bringing Kansas, Steve Hackett, Big Big Train and Asia aboard a floating festival devoted to everything from classic symphonic rock to adventurous modern progressive metal. Sailing from Miami on April 2, 2027, the cruise will visit Cozumel, Harvest Caye and Costa Maya before returning on April 8. With more than 30 acts, intimate artist experiences, late-night jam sessions and even a chance for passengers to perform themselves, the event offers something considerably more immersive than a conventional rock festival.
For progressive rock enthusiasts, the headlining lineup alone presents an impressive range of musical history.

Kansas have spent decades combining intricate instrumental arrangements with powerful rock songwriting, becoming one of America’s most recognizable progressive rock groups. Their catalogue helped introduce elaborate compositions, violin-driven melodies and shifting musical structures to audiences well beyond the genre’s traditional following.

Steve Hackett brings another essential piece of progressive rock history to the cruise. The former Genesis guitarist has maintained an extensive solo career while continuing to celebrate the music he helped create during the band’s influential 1970s period.

His performances have long appealed to fans interested in adventurous guitar playing, orchestral textures and the elaborate compositions that helped establish progressive rock as a distinct musical tradition.
Big Big Train represent another generation of the genre, drawing from classic British progressive rock while developing their own detailed arrangements and storytelling.
Asia provide a different perspective on that history, combining the technical abilities of musicians associated with progressive rock’s biggest groups with the melodic instincts of arena rock.

Biohaven shares pop as FDA accepts resubmission for ataxia drug with adcomm expected
sum: Troriluzole, in development for spinocerebellar ataxia, was rejected nearly a year ago when the FDA took issue with the design of Biohaven’s registrational study. The agency has now agreed to review a new application and render a decision in the first quarter of 2027.

Shares of Biohaven popped by as much as 36% on Thursday morning after the company disclosed the FDA’s acceptance of a resubmission for troriluzole—which the agency rejected late last year—in the rare, degenerative disorder spinocerebellar ataxia.

The FDA has assigned a new action date for troriluzole—also known as Vyglxia—in the first quarter of next year, according to a Thursday SEC filing. The agency also intends to hold an advisory committee meeting for the application, according to the document. A date for the adcomm will be set “in the near term.”

“The Vyglxia AdCom will be the most de-risking event here,” William Blair wrote to investors Thursday morning, citing the FDA’s previous reluctance to accept Biohaven’s three-year real-world evidence trial. Coined study 206-RWE, the program compared troriluzole to a natural history database on a movement scale modified for spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) as primary evidence to support effectiveness.
SCA is a group of rare diseases that lead to the progressive loss of control over movement. Many types of the disease are genetic and there is currently no cure.

The FDA issued a complete response letter (CRL) for troriluzole’s use in SCA in November 2025, citing “issues that can be inherent to real-world evidence and external control studies including potential bias” and spurring a contentious reaction from Biohaven.

“We are extremely disappointed on behalf of patients by this action from the Office of Neuroscience at FDA,” CEO Vlad Coric said in a statement following the rejection. “Beyond substantial evidence of safety and efficacy, patients with rare diseases also deserve an efficient, fair and flexible regulatory process that aligns with the urgency of their high unmet medical needs.”

sum: Progressive (PGR) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this insurer have returned +7.2%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.7% change. During this period, the Zacks Insurance - Property and Casualty industry, which Progressive falls in, has gained 4.1%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Why Progressive (PGR) Stock Is Up Today
sum: Shares of insurance company Progressive (NYSE:PGR) jumped 3.1% in the afternoon session after Morgan Stanley upgraded the insurer to 'Equal-weight' from 'Underweight' and raised its price target, citing strong performance relative to the sector. The investment bank boosted its price target on the stock to $210 from $190 per share.

Analysts noted that while the broader insurance industry faces challenging growth, Progressive's premium growth is "notably better" than the rest of the sector. The upgrade also follows a recent decline in the company's share price, which the firm said "represents a reset on valuation," suggesting the stock is now more fairly valued.
The shares closed the day at $213.84, up 3.3% from the previous close.
Is now the time to buy Progressive? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

Progressive's shares are not very volatile and have only had 5 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 10 days ago when the stock dropped 3.3% on the news that JPMorgan downgraded the insurance company's stock to Neutral from Overweight, citing valuation concerns. The investment bank set a price target of $250 for Progressive's shares. In the note, JPMorgan's analyst stated that although Progressive has the best underwriting track record among personal auto insurers due to its data analytics and pricing sophistication, the stock is now considered fully valued. sum: Progressive Corp (PGR) moved down by 3.15%. The Insurance sector is down by 1.26%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Progressive Corp (PGR) down 3.15%; Chubb Ltd (CB) down 1.95%; Aon PLC (AON) down 2.35%.

Progressive Corporation has experienced a notable decline in share price following the release of its latest monthly earnings report, which provided a granular look at company performance through the end of June. The primary catalyst appears to be a deterioration in the combined ratio, a critical metric for underwriting profitability. Investors reacted to higher than anticipated catastrophe losses stemming from severe weather events across the United States during the early summer months. These losses typically pressure the bottom line in the short term, leading to an immediate reassessment of quarterly earnings expectations.

Furthermore, broader macroeconomic concerns regarding loss cost inflation continue to weigh on the property and casualty insurance sector. While the company has been aggressive in implementing rate increases to offset rising claims costs, the most recent inflationary data suggests that auto repair expenses and medical costs remain stubbornly high. This creates a challenging environment where the pace of premium growth must continuously outrun the escalating costs of settling claims. Market participants are increasingly wary that the peak of the current hardening market cycle may be approaching, limiting the potential for further margin expansion.

Institutional sentiment has also been dampened by a shift in analyst forecasts. Several prominent brokerage firms have adjusted their near term outlooks, citing concerns over the sustainability of recent profit margins if frequency and severity trends do not normalize. The volatility seen today is indicative of a broader rotation out of defensive financial stocks as investors weigh the risks of persistent inflation against the backdrop of potential shifts in Federal Reserve policy.

From an operational standpoint, while Progressive continues to gain market share through its robust direct to consumer model and advanced data analytics, the immediate focus remains on its ability to manage the volatility of its underwriting results.

Progressive (PGR) Stock Looks Near Fair Value Following Leadership Changes
sum: Track your investments for FREE with Simply Wall St, the portfolio command center trusted by over 7 million individual investors worldwide.

Progressive stock has delivered a strong 149.4% gain over the past five years, yet on today's numbers it looks roughly in line with what many investors might consider a fair price rather than a clear bargain or an obvious excess.
- A 149.4% return over five years shows Progressive has already rewarded long term holders, which naturally raises the bar for any new value opportunity from here.

- Recent coverage pointing to underwriting discipline, profitability and balance sheet strength can support the current valuation, while exposure to catastrophe losses and execution risk around leadership changes may cap how much investors are willing to pay.
- With Progressive scoring 3 out of 6 on our valuation checks, the stock screens as a mixed picture rather than clearly cheap or clearly expensive.
The issue now is whether Progressive's current share price fairly reflects that track record and risk profile, or if the recent pullback has quietly rebuilt some value for patient investors.

The P/E ratio is a useful lens for Progressive because earnings power is central to how investors judge insurers. Progressive currently trades on a P/E of 11.0x, compared with an industry average of about 11.8x and a peer average of 8.3x, which puts the stock at a modest premium to closer peers but slightly below the wider insurance group.

items.t: PODCAST: Karishma Manzur Says NH Is Ready For a Real Progressive in US Senate
sum: All the progressives running in Democratic primaries aren’t in New York City. Dr. Karishma Manzur is bringing her “People’s Campaign” to the Democratic NH U.S. Senate primary taking on U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas.

In an extensive conversation wth NHJournal’s Michael Graham, Manzur explains her support for single-payer healthcare, ending U.S. support for Israel and her views on the success of Democratic Socialist candidates in the party.
Then another round of Rank Punditry with Dr. Dante Scala of UNH and veteran GOP operative Chuck McGee, who break down the current state of the federal races in New Hampshire.
